paths.description: Homepage/listing template: primary discovery surface, navigation, preferences, mobile reflow, performance, privacy and crawler behavior.
British Models category: representative long listing template; other demographic/tag listings share this template and were de-duplicated.
Live model detail: representative media/chat/age-gated core destination.
Signup: representative account-creation form and consent/terms surface; no account was created.
Login: authentication, recovery, federation, passwordless and autofill surface.
Invalid route: representative HTTP/navigation recovery state.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the default light page; the DOM reports color-scheme: normal and the stylesheet probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control and media-placeholder colors.

findings.summary: Non-essential animation is not reduced when requested.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-reduced-motion probes both report two 250 ms animations, and the stylesheet probe found no reduced-motion media query.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transition and animation rules in a no-preference query and disable or shorten them under reduce.

findings.summary: The page does not adapt to increased-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rule; the contrast-conditioned screenshot remains unchanged, while Lighthouse identifies foreground/background failures as low as 2.55:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations and preserve visible borders, text, focus and controls.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use view transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/source probe found no view-transition declarations on this multi-page browsing experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document view transitions for same-origin category, listing and detail navigation, with reduced-motion opt-out.

findings.summary: Persistent chrome does not react to scroll position.
findings.evidence: The long listing keeps fixed header/banner chrome, and CSS inspection found no scroll-state or scroll-progress implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce or adapt persistent chrome once content scrolls, preferably with scroll-state container queries and a stable fallback.

findings.summary: Menus and transient controls lack anchor-positioning support.
findings.evidence: The site exposes header/menu overlays, but the CSS probe found no anchor-name, position-anchor or fallback-position rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor menus and transient overlays to their trigger with position-try fallbacks, retaining the current positioning as fallback.

findings.summary: Stacked age and cookie prompts obscure primary content on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360×800 screenshot shows a 116 px age banner plus a fixed cookie panel covering the lower model cards on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve one compact, non-overlapping notice area and keep consent controls content-first and dismissible.

findings.summary: The cookie prompt behaves as custom fixed chrome rather than a clearly dismissible semantic primitive.
findings.evidence: The initial screenshot shows a fixed consent panel with Manage and Accept All but no direct dismiss/reject action; the DOM probe found popover=0.
findings.suggestedFix: Use an appropriately labelled dialog or popover with keyboard-safe focus and equivalent accept/reject/manage actions.

findings.summary: Navigation and notices consume a large share of the first mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Before the first complete content row, the mobile view spends 212 px on two nav rows and age verification, while the cookie panel overlays another 115 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation and defer nonessential controls so the live listings dominate the viewport.

findings.summary: Responsive changes rely on viewport layouts rather than component-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show adaptation, but CSS inspection found no @container declarations despite cards/nav components appearing in differently sized contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt size container queries for reusable cards, navigation groups and banners while keeping a viewport fallback.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on many interactive elements.
findings.evidence: A programmatic focus walk found outline-style:none and box-shadow:none on the sampled navigation links; 123 of 160 rendered controls were also under 44 px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and verify target size/spacing on the actual mobile control set.

findings.summary: Loading performance misses the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.0 s, CLS 0.125 and TBT 650 ms; the independent trace measured LCP 4.46 s and 318 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP surface, reserve dynamic slots and defer noncritical scripts/data until after the first useful content.

findings.summary: Late content causes visible layout shift.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer measured CLS 0.1277, including a single 0.1276 shift at 3.7 s; all 36 audited images lacked width/height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve media and banner space with intrinsic dimensions or aspect-ratio and avoid inserting notices above loaded content.

findings.summary: JavaScript blocks the main thread during startup.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 650 ms TBT; the trace found four long tasks up to 172.6 ms, and the layout observer recorded 143 ms and 100 ms tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the bootstrap path, split long tasks, and schedule noncritical hydration, analytics and feed work by priority.

findings.summary: The critical load is large and dependency-heavy.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 163 requests and 2.57 MB transferred, including 463 KB of fonts and 1.35 MB of scripts; two VeryHigh stylesheets load before first content.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset fonts, reduce initial bundles and CSS, and preload only confirmed LCP-critical resources.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,148 KiB unused JavaScript and 124 KiB unused CSS; the largest bootstrap script transfers 724,642 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by route and interaction, remove legacy/duplicate bundles, and load player/analytics code only when needed.

findings.summary: Important links and account inputs lack accessible names or labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name for model-card anchors. Signup/login probes found username, email and password fields with no label or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each card link a model-specific accessible name and associate visible labels with every account input.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple failures, including Join Free at 2.58:1, age-banner copy at 2.55:1 and the 18+ highlight at 2.74:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and re-test every state.

findings.summary: Focus visibility is missing across navigation.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reported no outline and no box shadow for the sampled focused links, preventing keyboard users from tracking position.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a consistent :focus-visible ring with sufficient contrast and test a complete keyboard traversal on all archetypes.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found width and height missing on all 36 images, even though the document otherwise has a valid HTML doctype and UTF-8 charset.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or a stable aspect-ratio for each image and retain responsive CSS sizing.

findings.summary: The runtime has platform hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three deprecated API warnings, inspector issues, a BFCache blocker and third-party-cookie use.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or isolate the offending challenge/third-party code, resolve inspector issues and eliminate avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript crawlers receive almost none of the listing content.
findings.evidence: The discoverability primitive received HTTP 403, measured 5% raw/rendered word coverage, and classified the response as a JS shell; title, H1 and description were absent from raw HTML. Lighthouse also failed crawlable-anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful listing content and metadata, return a successful crawlable response to legitimate bots, and keep card links as real named anchors.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent for the audited host.
findings.evidence: The page at xham.live declares https://xhamsterlive.com/ canonical, while /sitemap.xml returns 404; robots.txt otherwise allows the public paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose and document the canonical host, redirect alternates consistently, and publish a sitemap matching canonical URLs.

findings.summary: Share metadata has no preview image.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found an Open Graph title/description but an empty og:image value; one JSON-LD block is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide an accurate absolute preview image and validate Open Graph and JSON-LD against visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are missing; the cookie audit reports 25 cookies without Secure, including long-lived experiment cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Roll out a nonce/hash CSP, nosniff and Secure cookie defaults; retain SameSite/HttpOnly according to purpose.

findings.summary: The initial page has a broad third-party and fingerprinting footprint.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 148 of 163 requests and 2.43 of 2.57 MB to third-party origins; the DOM loads FingerprintJS and the tracker probe sees eight third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory each third party, remove fingerprinting/nonessential calls, gate optional analytics on consent, and batch remaining events.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are mostly absent.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no CSP, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or nosniff; only HSTS was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy report-only then enforced CSP, clickjacking protection, strict referrer policy and least-privilege permissions policy.

findings.summary: Core public content does not progressively enhance from usable HTML.
findings.evidence: The raw/crawler response is a 403 JS shell with only 5% content coverage, while the browser-rendered page contains the listings and headings.
findings.suggestedFix: Return semantic server-rendered headings, listings and links, then hydrate enhancements without replacing core reachability.

findings.summary: Consent presents Accept All prominently without an equivalent Reject action.
findings.evidence: Every captured page shows a green Accept All button and a lower-emphasis Manage action, but no Reject All control at the same level.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent Accept All, Reject All and Manage choices and persist the user’s choice without nagging.

findings.summary: Account fields do not expose useful autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: Signup has username/email inputs without labels and with autocomplete off/empty; login username and password fields have empty autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use stable names and autocomplete=username, email, current-password or new-password as appropriate, with visible labels.

findings.summary: Listing images are not delivered responsively.
findings.evidence: Of 36 images, 36 lack intrinsic dimensions, 22 lack srcset, 13 are more than 2× display width, 15 below-fold images are not lazy and 15 use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources, intrinsic dimensions and lazy loading below the fold.

findings.summary: Unused scripts and startup work consume unnecessary resources.
findings.evidence: The page transfers 1.35 MB of script and Lighthouse estimates 1,148 KiB is unused, alongside 46 XHR/fetch requests in the initial HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load player, analytics and route code, reduce polling and defer background fetches until user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 148 requests and 2.43 MB, or about 95% of transferred bytes; 2.12 MB comes from assets.chapturist.com alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request/byte budget, self-host critical assets where appropriate, and defer noncritical third-party code.

findings.summary: Repeated full-list scrolling retains a materially larger heap.
findings.evidence: A prewarmed full-scroll heap was 61.2 MB/1.27M nodes; after 10 down/up cycles it was 73.2 MB/1.58M nodes, about 19.5% more bytes and 24.7% more nodes. Separate browser runs and intentional caches lower confidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat the test in one instrumented session with explicit GC, then inspect retaining paths and cap list/cache growth if the increase persists.

taskList.title: Server-render crawlable core listings and normalize canonical/indexing signals
Cut and defer initial JavaScript, requests and third-party work
Deploy CSP, browser policies and secure cookie defaults
Fix accessible names, labels, focus and color contrast
Reserve image space and deliver responsive, lazy modern images
Add equal Reject All consent and reduce stacked first-load prompts
Honor dark, reduced-motion and contrast preferences
Verify and eliminate retained heap growth across repeated scrolling
Modernize navigation transitions and component positioning/responsiveness
Resolve deprecated APIs, inspector issues and BFCache blockers
